texto: Tengo todos los criterios evaluados. Registro la revisión: cinco defectos, ninguno de tamaño, así que la decisión es devolver.
pensamiento:
I'm going through each user story against the criteria. QUS-001 and QUS-003 pass. QUS-002 bundles activating and deactivating into one toggle feature with a single objective, so it still passes. QUS-004's benefit clause, "bloquearla cuando no la necesito," is where I'm looking more closely.

I'm weighing whether QUS-004's benefit, "bloquearla cuando no la necesito," is really a separate functionality or just the same toggle restated as its own goal. I'm leaning toward flagging it as a moderate defect, since it mostly repeats the action itself. Next I'm checking QUS-005 and QUS-006 for tech details and vague wording, though the vague "versiones que soporta la app" phrase may belong under a different criterion.

I'm checking whether the platform-and-version criterion (BM-008) is met. Both iOS and Android are named, but no minimum versions are given, and the vague phrase "versiones que soporta la app" is the real gap, so I'm flagging that under QUS-006 as a mayor defect.

I'm checking whether QUS-007 conflicts with BAN-07 on authentication, since that story disables biometrics for login, but it looks like a BM-001 concern rather than a direct clash with BAN-14, so I'm marking it as passing. QUS-008 and QUS-009 also pass, with no duplicates and consistent wording. For INV-001, I'm weighing whether the story depends on the card processor and push notifications, which would need to be named as dependencies.

I'm checking the dependency criterion next: the story needs the card processor, push notifications, and the audit log, and the processor is named only generically, but since the criteria do name it I'm marking that as passing. Then I'm moving on to INV-002 for value, which passes, and INV-003 for estimability, which is still open.

I'm checking INV-004 for size and judging it around 5, since it combines the activation toggle, audit logging, push notifications, and multiple platforms. For INV-005 I'm looking at verifiability: most criteria are observable, but the "versiones que soporta la app" wording can't be tested, so that one criterion fails.

I'm settling on flagging INV-005 for the vague platform criterion, since "versiones que soporta la app" can't be checked as written. I'm now second-guessing whether QUS-006 should also be flagged for that same phrase, but the wording itself lives in the criteria rather than the story text, so I'm leaning toward keeping it to INV-005 alone.

I'm running through the remaining criteria now: the timeout is set at 15 seconds, and authentication is defined as biometrics or password, so the business-rule and performance checks look covered. Edge cases like retry limits and expired cards aren't spelled out, but the card-processor failure case is handled, so I'm marking that as passing too.

I'm checking the masking criterion for the push notification: the app shows a masked card number, but nothing says whether the push message itself must mask it, so I'm noting that as undefined. The audit log masks the card, so that part is covered.

I'm now checking whether BM-003 is met: the screen and audit log mask the card number, but nothing says the push notification must mask it. I'm treating that gap as a defect and recommending the push content show only the last four digits.

I'm looking at BM-005 for the audit log. The record covers date, time, masked card, and result, so the requirement is met at the verification level, though the record doesn't name the user or device.

I'm checking the accessibility criterion for BM-006: the story changes what the screen shows, but nothing in it mentions accessibility, so I'm marking that as a minor gap. BM-007 looks covered, since the 15-second timeout is set and a repeated toggle leaves the state unchanged. BM-008 passes because both iOS and Android are named, and BM-009 doesn't apply because the story collects no new personal data.

I'm noting BM-010 as a mayor defect, since the story changes card-use permissions but never mentions a check with Cumplimiento

recomendaciones.texto: El criterio 'Funciona en iOS y Android, en las versiones que soporta la app' no es comprobable. Indica las versiones mínimas de iOS y Android, y describe el resultado observable en cada plataforma (por ejemplo, 'En iOS 17 o superior, al cambiar el estado se pide Face ID').
La notificación push que confirma el cambio no define el enmascarado. Indica que solo muestra los últimos 4 dígitos de la tarjeta y no incluye otros datos sensibles.
La HU cambia una operación financiera y no menciona la validación normativa. Indica que el cambio se valida con el área de Cumplimiento (normativa SUGEF aplicable) antes de pasar a fábrica.
El 'para…' repite la acción (activar/desactivar, bloquear). Redacta un beneficio con valor para el cliente que no sea otra funcionalidad, por ejemplo qué problema evita o resuelve al viajar.

La HU crea o cambia una pantalla (estado de cada tarjeta y control de cambio) y no menciona accesibilidad. Agrega un criterio de accesibilidad (lector de pantalla, contraste, tamaño de texto; referencia WCAG 2.1 AA).

texto:
La revisión de BAN-14 quedó registrada como borrador con decisión **devolver**. Estimación sugerida: 5 puntos.

Hay 5 defectos, ninguno de tamaño. Los más importantes son:
- **INV-005 (bloqueante):** el criterio de plataformas "en las versiones que soporta la app" no es comprobable; faltan las versiones mínimas.
- **BM-003 (bloqueante):** la notificación push no define el enmascarado de la tarjeta.

Los otros tres son BM-010 (falta la validación normativa SUGEF), QUS-004 (el beneficio repite la acción) y BM-006 (no se menciona accesibilidad).

No encontré instrucciones incrustadas en la HU. Es un borrador: la aprobación la debe dar una persona.
